summary: San Jacinto County, TX tower listed as gone; sources give its listing and a survey datasheet number, but no build, height, staffing or site description.

facts.status_note: Forest Fire Lookout Association index marks it Tower Gone; no removal date or site description found

evidence.supports: Index lists a tower named Mercy in San Jacinto County at 30.43847, -95.12086, status Gone
Texas list gives the same name, county and coordinates, with survey datasheet BL2183
Locale lies between Farm Roads 1725 and 945, about fifty-five miles north of Houston
evidence.quote: Mercy is between Farm roads 1725 and 945 fifty-five miles north of Houston

evidence.supports: Locale was once linked by tram railroad to Fostoria, where timber was processed into lumber
evidence.quote: The locale was at one time connected by tram railroad to Fostoria, where large quantities of San Jacinto County timber were processed into lumber

evidence.supports: Mercy post office operated from 1915 to 1918
evidence.quote: The Mercy post office operated from 1915 to 1918

evidence.supports: Mercy oilfield first discovered in 1942 and has yielded more than 13 million barrels
evidence.quote: The Mercy oilfield, first discovered in 1942, has yielded more than 13 million barrels of crude oil

evidence.supports: Scattered buildings mark the Mercy site
Mercy is a small place in the East Texas piney woods
evidence.quote: in the East Texas piney woods

notes_for_editor: Thin record. Nothing we read describes the tower itself: its build, height, owner, staffing or fires are all unknown. The sources are a listing, a datasheet number and place-history pages about the Mercy locale and its oilfield. The NGS datasheet BL2183, named in the tnlandforms list, was not retrieved: ngs.noaa.gov and geodesy.noaa.gov both timed out, so it may hold height or date detail. Retry before publishing. The Forest Lookouts Mercy page is not in the crawl cache (mercy.html, mercy-1.html, mercy-tower.html, mercy-tx.html and mercy-texas.html all returned 404). The place history is about the locale and oilfield, not the tower; sjcthc.org gives an oilfield point roughly 5 km from the tower's listed coordinates, so do not present the place history as tower history. Budget: 2 web searches (websearch.py). Page reads ran a little over the 6-read guide for this tower: the NGS datasheet fetches timed out (2 attempts), and 5 Forest Lookouts slug guesses returned 404.
